title: Resume tailoring check
summary: A fit result for one target role: each job requirement mapped to the master history (direct, adjacent or none) and to the tailored resume, before and after, with the requirements the history does not meet. A truth check confirms every line traces to the master resume; a format check covers parsing and length. The candidate tailors the resume; Sasha maps, scores and checks it, and the candidate approves the result.

values.label: Partial fit: some required items are gaps
Weak fit: most required items are gaps
Fix first: a line does not trace to the master

notAssessed: How a particular employer's applicant tracking system scores the resume
Tailoring itself (spec step 4): the workflow does not rewrite or propose lines; it checks a resume the candidate has already tailored
notes: Departure from the spec: there is no Tailor step yet. The candidate tailors the open resume; Sasha maps the master history (before), scores the open resume (after), and checks truth and format. The checkpoint approves the resume and its flags, not a list of changed lines.
The fit is Sasha's estimate for comparing versions; employers screen differently.
Report gaps plainly and handle them in the cover letter; the requirement map is saved with the run for the cover letter workflow.
CV variant: no length limit; publications, grants and teaching follow the field's usual order.

inputs.help: Link the master resume or full work history; it is the source of truth for every fact.

config.question: Does the master resume or work history show this requirement directly, show something adjacent, or not at all? Quote the evidence. Use only the master history, not the posting.
config.instructions: This maps the candidate's history to the role. A requirement the history cannot meet is a gap to report, not a fault in the resume.

config.question: Does the tailored resume show this requirement, early and in the posting's terms where the experience matches? Quote the line.

config.instructions: List each employer, job title, date range, degree, certification, skill and number (metric, count, amount) the resume states, with the line it appears in.

fields.label: Kind
fields.description: What sort of fact it is

config.question: Does the master resume or work history contain this fact exactly (titles and dates unchanged, numbers the same)? Compare against the master, never the posting.

checks.label: Before: required items with direct evidence
Before: required items with adjacent evidence
Before: required items with no evidence (gaps)
Before: preferred items with direct evidence
After: required items that are gaps
Estimated pages (compare with the field's norm; a CV has no limit)

checklist.label: Single column, real text
checklist.question: Is the content in a single column of real text, with nothing essential in tables, images, text boxes, headers or footers?

checklist.label: Standard headings
checklist.question: Are the section headings standard (Experience, Education, Skills and so on)?

checklist.label: Consistent dates
checklist.question: Are dates in one consistent format, with no unexplained overlaps?

checklist.label: Length suits the field
checklist.question: Is the length suited to the field and seniority (usually one to two pages for a resume; a CV has no limit)?

checklist.label: Results, not duties
checklist.question: Do the experience bullets state actions and results, keeping the numbers the master gives?

config.guidance: Give the match score as the computed counts state it (do not recount): required items met, partly met and gaps, and preferred items met, before (master history) and after (tailored resume). Judge the fit on the after counts: strong_fit when no required item is a gap; partial_fit when some are; weak_fit when more than half are. fact_mismatch when any fact does not trace to the master. List the gaps plainly and suggest handling them in the cover letter.

guards.reason: a line that does not trace to the master resume must be fixed before the resume is used.

config.instructions: The resume is your statement. Read it against the requirement map and approve it, and fix or remove any line the truth check flagged before using it.
